item.text: Write a fictional status report for Project Lantern 10, a pretend community-library appointment pilot. Use plain ASCII English only. Target 17000 characters (approximately 2833 words). Write 10 dated report entries in chronological order, with about 1700 characters per entry. Describe concrete fictional scope, earlier testing, a discovered cancellation-flow gap, its repair, evidence limitations, and a pending Captain decision about a pretend internal trial. Keep all names and facts fictional. State what would happen if the trial is postponed. Include mundane test details to reach the requested length. Output the complete report, not a summary. PROJECT LANTERN 10 - STATUS REPORT SERIES
Community Library Appointment Scheduling Pilot
Fictional Project Documentation

================================================================================
ENTRY 1 - 2026-09-03
Report Period: August 25 - September 2, 2026
Status: On Track

Project Lantern 10 launched its initial phase on August 25 with a focused scope: develop and test a web-based appointment scheduling system for three fictional library branches in the Greenbrook Metro system. The pilot targets library patrons seeking in-person reference consultations with trained staff members. The three participating branches are Central Greenbrook (65 staff slots per week), Riverside Branch (42 slots), and North End Library (38 slots), totaling 145 weekly available appointment windows.

The core technical scope includes a patron-facing booking interface, a staff-side view for appointment confirmation and notes, cancellation and rescheduling capabilities, notification delivery via email, and administrator dashboards for utilization reporting. The system runs on fictional technology: a Django 4.2 backend connected to PostgreSQL 15, with a React 18 frontend hosted through Vercel. Authentication uses OAuth 2.0 integration with the existing Greenbrook Library System identity provider.

Early testing commenced with unit test coverage across appointment creation, availability checking, and email notification generation. The backend achieved 84% code coverage on critical paths after initial test writing. The frontend passed basic interaction tests for the booking calendar view, form submission validation, and error state handling. No critical blockers identified in the first week.

Stakeholder alignment confirmed with library directors from all three branches on August 30. They confirmed current waiting list lengths: Central Greenbrook averages 18 pending requests, Riverside has 12, North End has 8. Directors estimated that 60 percent of cancellations occur with less than 48 hours notice currently. The pilot aims to reduce last-minute gaps through automated cancellation handling.

Technical team members assigned: backend development led by Marcus Chen, frontend development led by Sarah Okonkwo, QA and testing led by James Morrison, and project coordination by Patricia Valencia. First integration testing scheduled to begin September 5. No resource constraints anticipated at this stage. All team members have library systems domain experience from prior projects.

================================================================================
ENTRY 2 - 2026-09-10
Report Period: September 3 - September 9, 2026
Status: On Track

Integration testing commenced as scheduled on September 5 with a focus on end-to-end flows from patron login through appointment confirmation. The complete user journey for booking a new appointment was tested across all three branches simultaneously. Test data included 240 mock patron accounts and 480 pre-created appointment slots distributed across the three weeks of testing.

The appointment creation flow validated successfully. Patrons logged in using test OAuth credentials, viewed available time slots by branch preference, selected a 45-minute window, and received confirmation emails within 2 minutes of booking. Email delivery reliability measured at 98.4 percent on 234 test bookings. Three confirmations failed due to fictional email gateway throttling, which was expected in the test environment. The backend recorded all bookings in PostgreSQL with timestamps, patron identifiers, and staff assignments.

Staff-side confirmation interface testing revealed minor UI inconsistencies. Staff members viewed their assigned appointments in a daily and weekly view. The weekly view displayed correctly, showing all 145 slots across three branches with patron names, contact information, and reference request summaries. The daily view showed only 18 of 24 expected appointments on September 6. Investigation identified a timezone conversion bug: the daily view was retrieving appointments in UTC while displaying times in Eastern Time without proper offset calculation. Marcus Chen deployed a patch on September 7 that corrected the timezone handling. Retesting on September 8 confirmed the daily view now displays all scheduled appointments.

Email notification content testing passed for both patron and staff messages. Patrons received appointment confirmation with date, time, location, and cancellation instructions. Staff members received advance notices 24 hours before scheduled appointments. No formatting errors or missing information detected across 156 test email messages reviewed.

Administrator dashboard reporting was tested with synthetic utilization data. The dashboard displayed appointment fill rates by branch, cancellation rates by day of week, and no-show tracking (a feature enabled by staff marking attendance after appointments). Initial reports generated correctly on September 8. Dashboard load times measured at 340 milliseconds for weekly utilization views, well within the 1000-millisecond performance target.

Known issue: cancellation flow testing incomplete. The team began testing patron-initiated cancellations on September 9 but encountered workflow gaps that require further investigation. The testing showed that when a patron cancels an appointment, the system correctly records the cancellation timestamp and marks the slot as available. However, the process for reassigning the freed time slot and notifying the patron of the cancellation completion lacks clarity. James Morrison documented the gap and flagged it for priority review in the next testing cycle.

No other blockers identified. Team velocity on track with implementation phase. Remaining work: finalize cancellation flow, complete rescheduling logic, validate notification escalation for confirmed appointments with attendance tracking, and conduct user acceptance testing with actual library staff.

================================================================================
ENTRY 3 - 2026-09-17
Report Period: September 10 - September 16, 2026
Status: Blocked - Cancellation Flow Gap

The cancellation flow gap identified on September 9 expanded significantly during testing on September 10-13. Detailed investigation revealed multiple unhandled scenarios within the cancellation and rescheduling workflow that differ from initial requirements.

The discovered gaps are as follows: When a patron initiates cancellation through the web interface, the system generates a cancellation request record, records the timestamp, and marks the slot as available. However, staff members were not notified of the cancellation automatically. This is critical because staff at Greenbrook branches currently rely on confirmation calls one day before appointments; without cancellation notification, staff could prepare materials for appointments that no longer exist. A patron cancellation at 10:30 AM would result in staff discovering the gap only when the patron fails to arrive at the scheduled time.

Second gap: when a patron clicks the cancellation confirmation button, the system asks whether the patron wants to be offered alternative appointment times. If the patron selects yes, the system must gather new preference information (preferred date range, time of day, branch preference, and reason for rescheduling). The current interface collected this data in the confirmation dialog but did not persist it for later matching. The system would acknowledge the patron's preference without actually scheduling a follow-up or notifying the scheduler to prioritize that patron.

Third gap: cancellation reasons were not being captured. Library directors indicated on September 12 that understanding why patrons cancel is important for service improvement. The current cancellation form did not include a reason dropdown or text field. Patricia Valencia flagged this as a design requirement that was omitted during initial scoping.

Fourth gap: the system lacked a confirmation message showing patrons that cancellation had completed successfully. Patrons clicked the cancellation button, and the form submitted, but no success state message appeared. Testers could not confirm whether the cancellation was processed or the transaction had failed. This is a user experience failure that could lead to duplicate cancellation attempts or patron confusion.

Testing volume on cancellation scenarios was limited. James Morrison executed 34 manual cancellation tests: 18 for successful cancellations with no rescheduling request, 16 for cancellations with rescheduling preference indicated. Of the 18 successful cancellations, 3 failed silently (no success message), and the appointment was still marked as booked in the staff view despite the cancellation record existing in the database.

On September 13, Patricia Valencia scheduled a working session with Marcus Chen and Sarah Okonkwo to inventory all cancellation requirements and map the missing workflow states. The team documented five distinct cancellation scenarios that the system must handle:
1. Patron cancels, prefers no rescheduling, wants no further contact.
2. Patron cancels, wants to be rescheduled to a future appointment at library discretion.
3. Patron cancels, wants to remain on waiting list for specific future dates.
4. Patron cancels via phone through staff (staff-initiated on behalf of patron for no-show management).
5. System-initiated cancellation due to manual staff cancellation of appointment blocks (branch closed due to weather, staff illness, etc.).

The current implementation handles only scenario 1 partially. Scenarios 2-5 are either unimplemented or partially implemented with missing state transitions. This is a moderate scope increase but critical to the pilot's success.

Status escalated to blocked because cancellation flow repairs cannot be deferred to post-launch. Library directors confirmed on September 14 that cancellation is the single highest-traffic flow in their current system: of 145 weekly appointments, approximately 38 (26 percent) are cancelled or rescheduled weekly. Without correct cancellation handling, the pilot will increase staff burden rather than reduce it.

Repair plan initiated by Marcus Chen: redesign the cancellation API to support all five scenarios, redesign the patron-facing cancellation form with reason collection and success messaging, implement queue-based rescheduling for scenarios 2 and 3, and add staff notification for all patron cancellations. Estimated implementation time: 4 working days. Testing will require additional test cases for each scenario. No team member availability constraints; all three developers remain assigned.

Anticipated completion of cancellation flow repair: September 20. This will bring the overall project timeline to a one-week delay from the original September 15 go-live target.

================================================================================
ENTRY 4 - 2026-09-21
Report Period: September 17 - September 20, 2026
Status: Cancellation Flow Repair Complete - Testing Phase

Marcus Chen completed the cancellation flow redesign and implementation on schedule on September 20, one day ahead of the September 21 target. The implementation addressed all five cancellation scenarios identified in the previous report.

The redesigned cancellation API now distinguishes between patron-initiated and staff-initiated requests. Patron-initiated cancellations include a reason field (dropdown options: illness, schedule conflict, found alternative resource, other, prefer not to say) and a follow-up preference field (no rescheduling, rescheduled at discretion, keep on waiting list, contact later). The API validates that all required fields are provided before processing the cancellation request. Validation tests confirmed that missing reason or preference data triggers appropriate error responses on September 20.

Sarah Okonkwo updated the patron-facing cancellation form to include a success state. Patrons now see a confirmation message: "Your appointment has been cancelled. You may book a new appointment at any time." A cancel button also appears, allowing patrons to navigate back to the main booking interface. Form submission now includes explicit success and error feedback via modal dialog. Five different error states were tested: network failure, database write failure, email delivery failure, invalid appointment ID, and user authentication expiration during form submission.

The rescheduling queue system was implemented to handle cancellations where patrons request staff-discretionary rescheduling. When a patron cancels and selects "rescheduled at discretion," the cancellation is recorded with a flag in the database, and a scheduler notification is generated. Patricia Valencia reviewed the notification content on September 19. Scheduler notifications include patron name, reason for cancellation, preferred date range (if specified), and a link to view the patron's availability preferences. Notifications are routed to a fictional email address: greenbrook-schedulers@greenbrook.lib.

Staff-initiated cancellations were implemented to allow library staff to cancel appointments on behalf of patrons (for no-show management or branch closures). Staff access this through a separate admin panel with a dropdown to select the appointment to cancel and a reason field. The reason options for staff include: patron no-show, system closure, staff illness, facility issue, or patron request received via phone. Initial testing of the staff cancellation interface confirmed that all staff-initiated cancellations generate patron notifications (via email) within 5 minutes of the cancellation action.

Testing Phase Results (September 21-20): James Morrison executed 87 cancellation test cases across all five scenarios. Results: Scenario 1 (cancel, no rescheduling): 18 tests, 18 passed. Scenario 2 (cancel, staff-discretionary rescheduling): 19 tests, 18 passed, 1 failed due to email delivery timeout. Scenario 3 (cancel, remain on waiting list): 16 tests, 15 passed, 1 failed due to missing waiting list status update in the database. Scenario 4 (staff-initiated cancellation): 18 tests, 17 passed, 1 failed due to missing patron notification for a specific timezone edge case. Scenario 5 (system-initiated block cancellation): 16 tests, 15 passed, 1 failed due to incomplete cascade deletion of dependent appointments.

Total pass rate: 83 of 87 tests (95.4 percent). One test failure (waiting list status update) affects data integrity and requires priority remediation. Three test failures (email timeout, timezone notification, cascade deletion) are edge cases that should be handled but may not affect the core pilot functionality. Marcus Chen estimated 4 hours to fix the waiting list status bug and 2 hours per remaining failure for comprehensive edge case handling.

Evidence limitations: The testing environment does not fully simulate the actual load that the system will experience during pilot launch. No load testing was conducted on the cancellation flow with more than 50 concurrent cancellation requests. The team does not have data on whether the email delivery timeout observed in one test represents a systematic issue or an isolated network fluctuation. Database cascade deletion logic was tested with synthetic data but not validated against production schema complexity.

The team's confidence in the cancellation flow implementation is high for the primary scenarios (1-3), moderate for scenario 4 (staff-initiated), and lower for scenario 5 (system-initiated block cancellations). Recommendation from James Morrison: proceed with user acceptance testing for scenarios 1-3, defer scenario 5 to post-launch optimization, and treat scenario 4 as requires-caution until the timezone edge case is fully resolved.

Next Phase: User Acceptance Testing with actual library staff scheduled for September 24-26. Cancellation flow will be primary focus during UAT sessions. Team availability remains full; no resource constraints.

================================================================================
ENTRY 5 - 2026-09-27
Report Period: September 21 - September 26, 2026
Status: UAT Complete - Minor Issues, Ready for Internal Trial Decision

User Acceptance Testing (UAT) conducted September 24-26 with library staff from all three branches. Participants: 4 staff members from Central Greenbrook, 3 from Riverside, 2 from North End, totaling 9 library staff members. Testing duration: 6 hours per branch (18 hours total), conducted in actual library environments with live network connectivity.

UAT focus areas: patron booking flow, staff confirmation interface, cancellation workflow, and rescheduling process. Staff members were provided with test patron accounts and asked to guide fictional patrons through booking, confirmation, and cancellation processes. Staff also tested the daily and weekly appointment view interfaces and the administrator dashboard.

Results summary: Patron booking flow validated successfully. Staff confirmed that the interface matched their mental model of how the booking system should work. Time to complete a booking from login to confirmation averaged 3 minutes and 15 seconds across all 18 test bookings conducted by staff. No staff members reported confusion about the booking process.

Staff confirmation interface validated successfully. Staff members viewed their assigned appointments in both daily and weekly views without issue. The timezone correction implemented in September 7 was confirmed to be working correctly. Staff noted that the weekly view was more useful than the daily view for their workflow. Appointment details (patron name, reference request summary, contact information) were sufficient for preparation.

Cancellation workflow tested with 12 cancellation scenarios conducted by staff. All 12 cancellations processed successfully. Staff confirmed that the automated patron notifications (email) provided clear information about the cancellation. One staff member requested that cancellation notifications include a link for patrons to immediately rebook an appointment, rather than requiring them to restart the booking flow. This is a feature request for post-launch enhancement.

Rescheduling process tested with 8 patron-initiated rescheduling requests. Patrons cancelled appointments and indicated preference for staff-discretionary rescheduling. The system generated scheduler notifications as designed. Patricia Valencia reviewed the scheduler notifications with library directors on September 25. Directors confirmed that the notification content was clear and actionable. The fictional greenbrook-schedulers@greenbrook.lib inbox received 8 notifications corresponding to the 8 test cancellations, with no delays exceeding 6 minutes.

Minor issues identified during UAT: Two staff members reported that the appointment notes field was too small to capture detailed reference request information. The current character limit is 256 characters. Staff requested expansion to 500 characters minimum. This is a straightforward database schema and form field adjustment requiring minimal effort. Sarah Okonkwo estimated 1 hour to implement and test.

One Riverside staff member reported confusion about how to access the administrator dashboard. The navigation menu did not make the dashboard link sufficiently obvious. Sarah Okonkwo reviewed the navigation and added a dashboard link to the main staff menu. Usability issue resolved on September 26.

Central Greenbrook director requested automatic appointment reminders to patrons 24 hours before scheduled appointments. This is a feature expansion beyond current scope. A notification template was already prepared for staff-side 24-hour reminders; reversing that to notify patrons is feasible but requires additional implementation. Estimated effort: 3 hours for implementation and testing. Decision deferred to post-launch phase.

Testing confidence: Library staff confirmed through exit interviews that the system handles their core workflow correctly. The cancellation flow, validated as the highest-priority gap two weeks prior, is now functioning reliably in a realistic library setting. No critical blockers remain.

Evidence limitations: UAT was conducted with staff members in a controlled setting, not during actual patron appointments. No measurement of how patrons will actually interact with the system under real conditions. The system was tested with synthetic patron data, not real patron accounts or behaviors. Three of nine staff members had prior technology experience above the library median; their feedback may not represent all staff skill levels.

Team Status: All team members remain assigned. No resource constraints. Working tree prepared for internal trial launch. Code is staged and ready for deployment to trial environment on a fictional trial server infrastructure.

Captain Decision Required: The project now awaits a decision on whether to proceed with the internal trial phase. The internal trial will run the system with real patron appointments at one branch (Central Greenbrook) for a two-week period. If the trial is approved, projected launch is October 1. If postponed, the system enters a holding pattern until the next scheduled decision point.

Decision Impact - If Internal Trial Proceeds (October 1 start): Week 1 (October 1-7): Deployment to production-like trial environment, staff training at Central Greenbrook, system monitoring and log collection, live appointments scheduled. Week 2-3 (October 8-14): Continued live appointments, data collection on appointment patterns and cancellations, staff feedback collection, system observation. Week 4 (October 15-21): Data analysis, findings report preparation, decision on full pilot launch (all three branches) or adjustments. Timeline to full pilot launch: late October.

Decision Impact - If Internal Trial Is Postponed: The project enters a waiting state. The implemented system remains staged in the working tree. Team members can be reassigned to other projects or placed on on-call status for trial preparation. If trial is postponed for more than two weeks, the team recommends a second round of UAT with fresh staff participants to validate that the system remains correct after any team context switches. Estimated cost of two-week postponement: 2-3 additional days of preparation work when the trial resumes. Cost of one-month postponement: full UAT re-run recommended, estimated 5 additional days of work. System code remains valid for at least 30 days without dependency updates or environmental changes.

Team Recommendation: Proceed with internal trial. The system is functionally complete for the pilot scope, validated by library staff, and ready for real-world testing. Deferral risks lack of momentum and requires repeat validation work.

================================================================================
ENTRY 6 - 2026-10-01
Report Period: September 27 - October 1, 2026
Status: Internal Trial Phase Initiated

Internal trial launch approved on September 28. Deployment to the trial environment completed on September 30 without incident. Central Greenbrook branch went live with the appointment system on October 1 at 09:00 AM local time.

Deployment process: Marcus Chen migrated the database schema to the trial PostgreSQL instance on September 29. Database migration included all appointment tables, patron identity mappings, and historical test data was purged. The production-like trial environment mimics the actual server infrastructure the system will run on, with equivalent CPU, memory, and network configuration. Deployment included configuration of the fictional email gateway for patron and staff notifications.

Pre-launch checklist completed: Email delivery validation (3 test emails sent, 3 received), staff interface access verification (all 4 Central Greenbrook staff members logged in successfully), patron OAuth integration test (5 patron accounts created and authenticated), administrator dashboard access (Patricia Valencia confirmed reporting functions), and backup procedures validation (database backup executed, verified restoration on test instance).

Trial monitoring: Live appointment slots became available to patrons on October 1 at 09:00 AM. The first appointment was booked at 09:47 AM by a fictional patron (test patron ID retained for monitoring purposes). The second and third appointments were booked by actual patrons at 10:15 AM and 10:33 AM. By end of October 1, eight appointments had been booked across three available dates.

System performance monitoring confirmed: Backend API response times ranged from 180 milliseconds to 340 milliseconds for appointment creation requests. Database query times for availability checking averaged 45 milliseconds. Email delivery completed for all 8 patron confirmation messages within 3 minutes of appointment booking. No performance degradation observed.

Staff interaction: Three of four Central Greenbrook staff members logged into the staff interface on October 1 to view their assigned appointments. Daily view and weekly view displayed correctly. One staff member confirmed that an appointment booked at 09:47 AM was visible in the system within 2 minutes of the booking.

Email notifications: All 8 patron confirmations generated correctly with accurate appointment details (date, time, location, staff member name). Patron contact information was correctly associated with bookings. Email formatting rendered correctly in multiple email client software (tested in fictional Outlook, Gmail, Apple Mail interfaces).

Day 1 issues: None. System stability was nominal throughout October 1. No error logs generated for critical functions.

Traffic projection: Based on first-day volume (8 bookings), Central Greenbrook may expect 30-40 bookings per week during the trial period if traffic scales linearly. Historical data from library directors suggested 15-20 weekly appointment requests for this branch. The higher early volume may reflect novelty or promotional messaging to patrons about the new system. More data needed over the next week to establish accurate traffic patterns.

Trial monitoring plan: The team will collect system logs daily, monitor appointment booking rates, track cancellation requests, observe email delivery success rate, and gather staff feedback at the end of each week. Patricia Valencia scheduled a weekly check-in meeting with Central Greenbrook director for October 8.

Next milestone: One week of trial operation (October 1-7) will provide sufficient data to assess system stability and staff workflow integration. Cancellation testing during trial will be particularly valuable since the pilot discovered cancellation to be the most frequent transaction type.

Team status: All members assigned to trial monitoring and support on-call. No planned development work during trial unless critical issues emerge. System appears stable and ready for sustained operation.

================================================================================
ENTRY 7 - 2026-10-08
Report Period: October 1 - October 8, 2026
Status: Trial Week 1 Complete - System Stable, Moderate Traffic

First week of internal trial completed October 8. Central Greenbrook processed 34 appointments booked and 8 cancellations through the system during October 1-7.

Appointment booking volume: 34 appointments across 6 available dates during the trial week. Daily bookings ranged from 3 to 7, averaging 4.9 per day. This volume is approximately double the projected 30-40 per week estimate from October 1. Analysis suggests that patrons are catching up on prior waiting list demand (library directors reported 18 pending requests before trial launch) and testing the new system.

Cancellation volume: 8 cancellations out of 34 bookings represents a 23.5 percent cancellation rate. This is consistent with the historical 26 percent cancellation rate cited by library directors in September. Of the 8 cancellations: 4 were initiated by patrons online (scenarios 1-3), and 4 were phone-based requests that staff manually cancelled in the system (scenario 4, staff-initiated).

Cancellation reasons provided by patrons (captured in the form): Two patrons selected "schedule conflict," one selected "found alternative resource," one selected "other." These reasons were correctly recorded in the database and accessible to staff through the administrator dashboard.

Rescheduling requests: Of the 4 patron-initiated online cancellations, 2 patrons selected "staff-discretionary rescheduling" and 2 selected "no rescheduling." The 2 rescheduling requests generated scheduler notifications. Patricia Valencia observed that rescheduling requests were processed within 6 hours by library staff (who manually reviewed the notification inbox and sent staff-initiated rescheduling confirmations). This is faster than the historical phone-based rescheduling process, which typically took 1-2 business days.

System performance: Response times during peak booking hours (around 10:00 AM and 4:00 PM) remained within acceptable ranges. The longest observed API response time was 510 milliseconds during an 11:30 AM booking spike. Database performance remained stable with query times under 100 milliseconds for all appointment operations. Email delivery success rate remained at 98.4 percent during the week, consistent with early testing results.

Email delivery issues: One patron confirmation email failed to deliver on October 4 at 2:15 PM. The email address in the patron OAuth profile was invalid (fictional: "patron.garcia@invalid-email-domain"). The system correctly flagged the delivery failure in logs. Patricia Valencia manually contacted the patron through the library and provided appointment details verbally. This represents a data quality issue in the identity provider, not a system issue.

Staff interface usage: Staff members checked their appointment views daily. Two staff members reported that they accessed the weekly view on 5 of 6 working days (October 1, 2, 3, 5, 6). One staff member accessed the daily view on October 1 only. No staff member reported difficulty using the interface or confusion about appointment management.

Staff feedback summary (from October 8 check-in with branch director): Staff appreciated the automated patron confirmations, which reduced their manual confirmation call burden. One staff member reported that she previously spent approximately 3 hours per week on confirmation calls; this should decrease significantly now that patrons receive immediate automated confirmations. The branch director noted that the 4 phone-based cancellation requests that staff entered into the system took staff members 5-8 minutes each to process (including verifying patron identity over phone, confirming cancellation, and entering data into the system). The director will explore moving more cancellation requests to the online patron-initiated flow in coming weeks.

One staff concern: A staff member noted that patrons booking online do not provide detailed reference request information, making appointment preparation more difficult. Some patrons left the request notes field blank, while others provided only one or two words (e.g., "book search," "database help"). Historical phone-based booking included more detailed intake conversations. This is a workflow adaptation issue that will likely improve as patrons become more familiar with the online form.

Patron feedback: Patricia Valencia reviewed patron interactions through email and the system logs. Patrons did not report issues. One patron emailed a general question about appointment rescheduling procedures (answered within 2 hours). No patron complaints or technical support requests were received.

System monitoring: No error logs indicating critical system failures. No database integrity issues detected. All transactions (bookings, cancellations, rescheduling requests) were correctly recorded and accessible through the administrator dashboard.

Data collected during trial week 1: 34 appointment transactions, 8 cancellation transactions, 6 rescheduling-request notifications, 1 email delivery failure, 0 critical errors, 5 access sessions from each staff member.

Trial week 2 objectives: Continue monitoring appointment and cancellation volumes to establish stable traffic patterns. Encourage more patrons to book online (staff can mention the online system to phone-based callers). Monitor whether cancellation volume remains consistent. Gather detailed staff feedback on workflow changes. Prepare data report for late October full-pilot decision.

Team status: All members on support standby. No issues have required development intervention. System is operating as designed. Trial appears to be proceeding normally.

================================================================================
ENTRY 8 - 2026-10-15
Report Period: October 8 - October 15, 2026
Status: Trial Week 2 Complete - Data Sufficient for Decision, Minor Configuration Request

Trial week 2 (October 8-14) completed without incident. Central Greenbrook processed 38 appointments booked and 9 cancellations during this period.

Appointment booking volume: 38 new appointments booked during week 2, averaging 5.4 per day. This is a slight increase from week 1 (4.9 per day). The cumulative trial volume is 72 appointments across two weeks. The system is tracking toward approximately 30 appointments per week in steady state, which aligns with the library director's earlier estimate of historical demand.

Cancellation volume: 9 cancellations out of 38 bookings represents a 23.7 percent cancellation rate, nearly identical to week 1 (23.5 percent). The consistency in cancellation rate across two independent weeks suggests that this is a stable characteristic of patron behavior, not a random fluctuation. This rate matches historical expectations and validates the team's earlier analysis.

Cancellation flow performance: All cancellations processed correctly through the system. Patron-initiated online cancellations: 5. Staff-initiated phone-based cancellations: 4. Rescheduling requests: 3 patrons requested staff-discretionary rescheduling. Processing time for rescheduling requests remained fast (average 5 hours from cancellation notification to staff response).

Email performance: Email delivery success rate improved slightly to 98.9 percent (34 of 34 confirmations + 9 cancellation notifications delivered successfully, 1 failure due to invalid patron email address similar to week 1). The system is performing within design specifications.

Staff feedback (week 2 summary): Central Greenbrook director reported that staff are adapting to the system. Two staff members have become more efficient at appointment preparation by booking shorter preparation windows (previously they blocked out 1.5 hours per appointment for preparation; now they block 45 minutes after receiving confirmation immediately). The reference request information issue noted in week 1 shows slight improvement: patrons in week 2 provided more detailed notes on average (average word count in request notes field: week 1 was 3.2 words, week 2 was 4.8 words). This suggests that patrons are learning to provide better information.

One configuration request from staff: Central Greenbrook director requested that the appointment duration be configurable per staff member. Currently, all appointments are fixed at 45 minutes. Some staff members would prefer 30-minute slots for simpler requests, while others want 60-minute slots for complex research consultations. The current system treats all appointments as identical. This is a scope request outside the trial parameters. Patricia Valencia recorded the request for consideration during the full-pilot design phase.

System stability: No errors or performance issues. Database integrity validated. All transactions correctly recorded. Monitoring logs show no anomalies.

Trial data sufficiency assessment: James Morrison conducted a statistical analysis of the two weeks of trial data. With 72 total bookings and consistent patterns (cancellation rate stable, booking volume steady, system performance nominal), the team has sufficient evidence to support a decision on full-pilot launch. Additional data would provide marginal value for decision-making at this point.

Full-Pilot Scope Decision: The trial data supports proceeding with full pilot launch (all three branches simultaneously) on October 22. Deployment to Riverside Branch and North End Library would follow the same process as the Central Greenbrook trial: staging in production-like environment on October 18, staff training on October 19-20, and live launch on October 22.

Evidence limitations on full-pilot readiness: The trial ran at approximately 30 appointments per week, which is the expected steady-state volume. However, the system has not been tested at peak loads. If multiple branches experience simultaneous usage surges, system performance is unknown. No load testing was conducted with more than 50 concurrent users. The trial did not test scenario 5 (system-initiated block cancellations due to branch closure); this scenario remains unvalidated in production. The confirmation approach for system-initiated cancellations was designed but not exercised.

Risk assessment: Low risk of system failure during full-pilot launch based on trial performance. Moderate risk of workflow issues at Riverside and North End branches due to different staff configurations and patron populations (not yet using the system). Low risk of email delivery problems (98.9% success rate in trial). Unknown risk for scenario 5 (block cancellations).

Recommendation from technical team: Proceed with full-pilot launch on October 22. The trial has validated the core workflows. Continue monitoring as branches come online and escalate any issues that emerge. Maintain on-call support for the first week of each new branch launch.

Captain Decision Required: Approve full-pilot launch on October 22 (all three branches), or defer and collect additional trial data. Cost of deferral: one week delay pushes full-pilot launch to October 29 and post-pilot analysis to early November. Benefit of deferral: minimal based on current evidence sufficiency.

ENTRY 9 - 2026-10-22
Report Period: October 15 - October 22, 2026
Status: Full Pilot Launch Approved and Deployed

Captain approval for full-pilot launch received on October 16. Deployment to Riverside Branch and North End Library completed as planned.

Deployment process for new branches: Database schema and patron identity mappings were provisioned for both Riverside and North End on October 18. Central Greenbrook remained operational throughout. Staff training sessions were conducted on October 19-20: Riverside staff (3 members) trained on October 19, North End staff (2 members) trained on October 19 afternoon. Training focused on the staff interface, appointment confirmation workflow, and escalation procedures for issues. Duration: 1.5 hours per session. All staff members successfully logged into the system during training and confirmed they understood the workflow.

Central Greenbrook optimization: Live trial data informed a configuration change. Based on observation that patrons at Central Greenbrook are using the system reliably, appointment slot availability was expanded from 3 concurrent staff schedules to 4 concurrent schedules starting October 22. This increases weekly available slots from 65 to 87 at Central Greenbrook. The director confirmed this expansion aligns with historical demand.
